pr_body:
Retries should be an implementation detail of the cache client implementation. No client is interested in the number of retry attempts, so it seems better to make the retry code transparent with respect to exceptions. The retry code also wrapped arbitrary exceptions with RetryException. It is now the responsibility of the cache implementation code to convert low-level exceptions to IOException or an error meaningful at higher layers like CacheNotFoundException. For example, the gRPC action cache and remote executor now explicitly convert StatusRuntimeException into IOException.

Also, remove PassThroughException, since it's unused.

This should fix https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/6308.

issue_context.title: Incomprehensible error message: "Exhaused retry attempts"
issue_context.body:
https://buildkite.com/bazel/google-bazel-presubmit/builds/9914#140dc6c6-0034-485a-bf8d-6ba99f457241

```
ERROR: /Users/buildkite/builds/buildkite-imacpro-4-1/bazel/google-bazel-presubmit/src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/BUILD:1537:1: Couldn't build file src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/rules-tests.jar: Building src/test/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/rules-tests.jar (3 source files) and running annotation processors (AutoAnnotationProcessor, AutoValueProcessor) failed: Unexpected IO error.: Exhaused retry attempts (0)
```

What subsystem has exhausted the retries here? What did it try in the first place? 0 attempts? Really?
comments: In my case, it was because my Nginx config did not set keepalive_requests. @ola-rozenfeld, If that include "bf6a63d", it will just be a warning like error read from cache. But regardless, we should add a stacktrace for the error or warning.

A stacktrace should be available for all errors you use --verbose_failures. This is a warning, though, that's why we didn't think to include a stacktrace. Not sure stacktraces on warnings are a good experience in general...

This was an error before "bf6a63d", and use "--verbose_failures" did not generate more info or stacktrace, at least in my case. Usually this warning means there is cache miss and there is an issue with server setup, that's why a stacktrace would be very helpful.

I don't know whether the binary I used included that commit, but I'm not sure it matters - the message is useless, whether it's a warning or an error. It doesn't even mention the remote cache. An exception stack trace would at least tell me which part of Bazel it's in.

To add on that:
1.  If not include bf6a63d, use --verbose_failures does not generate a stacktrace, this is a bug
2. If include bf6a63d, the error becomes a warning, it is more deceiving. It makes you think your cache is working properly, but actually not.

So https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/bf6a63d64a010f4c363d218e3ec54dc4dc9d8f34 fixed the cryptic error message bug with no stack trace. However, I'm not sure if there are any remaining things that are wrong here. What should Bazel do when your remote cache doesn't work properly with local execution?
When we designed the feature, we thought that remote cache errors should not fail local builds. So all these errors are warnings, by design. Do you think that wasn't the right call? Or do you think we should include stack traces with the warnings if --verbose_failures is on?

Thanks for the detailed info. Yes, I agree that bazel remote should not fail the build.  Ideally, at the end of the build it should provide warning summary message how many attempted connections failed(and printout something like "your server most likely has issue"). And if you use --verbose_failures flag, it can provide stacktrace.
If everything is set right(correct me if I am wrong), we will mostly get 100% cache hit, so print out some thing like "your remote server most likely has issue", when it is less than 100% hit would be very helpful for people are not so familiar with bazel remote cache. As the remote cache miss are only warnings, if people can build successfully, they may not realize their server have problem, and will just go with it. In the end, they did not utilize the full strength of remote cache. For one example, I have seen in another opened issue that  a user has a lot of such warnings in their CI box, which I believe he did not set the remote server correctly.
Also, it would be helpful if we have a flag to specify the number of retries for get/put cache. Now it seems it only tries once.

We do have a few flags controlling the retry behavior, like
--experimental_remote_retry_max_attempts. They are only relevant to gRPC
remote cache, though. We don't retry the http cache currently.

review_comments: Please use `new IOException(e.getMessage(), e)`, else `IOException.getMessage()` will contain the `StatusRuntimeException` in the message.

Is the behavior bad? IMO, something like `IOException: StatusRuntimeException: UNAVAILABLE` is better than `IOException: UNAVAILABLE`.

I think if we want to have better error messages for specific cases, we should create more exceptions like `CacheNotFoundException` (e.g., `CacheDownException`) and produce nice error messages in the generic caching layer.
Looking at your example I'd argue that both are equally bad :-). Let's leave it as is and fix error messages as a follow up.
I think we can kill the `RemoteRetrier` class and just use `Retrier`?

We maybe could. It depends how much you want to keep `Retrier` generic. Even after this change, `RemoteRetrier.execute` encodes that application-specific logic that `IOException` and `InterruptedException` should be directly propagated while other exceptions should be wrapped in a `RuntimeException`.

There are several cleanups including removing `RemoteRetrier` we could make after this change. As you mention, this CL is already quite complex, so I'm reluctant to stick them in here.
